title: November: Blacking Out and Coming To
coreMove: A shopping ban survives a slip when the breach is named, the trigger is understood, and the rule resumes before shame can turn one mistake into permission to collapse.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who hide a lapse during a self-imposed rule
exampleSpecs.stakes: Secrecy can turn one breach into proof that the entire experiment has failed.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Name the mistake to the audience and return to the boundary.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who distrust strict personal rules
exampleSpecs.stakes: A fair objection can be dismissed too quickly, leaving the real relapse risk unmanaged.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Honor the skeptic's concern while distinguishing rules from shame.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who expect willpower to handle designed temptation
exampleSpecs.stakes: Urgency and scarcity language can make a private commitment feel foolish.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Plan for the predictable consumer event before it starts pressing.

exampleSpecs.audience: people maintaining a rule in front of others
exampleSpecs.stakes: A perfect image can turn accountability into performance and block useful repair.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the public thread to show the messy middle, not only the wins.

exampleSpecs.domain: household planning before a consumer holiday
exampleSpecs.audience: readers facing a known spending trigger
exampleSpecs.stakes: Without advance limits, cultural permission to buy can make restraint feel antisocial or wasteful.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Set the limit before the trigger-heavy day begins.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who convert one mistake into total failure
exampleSpecs.stakes: A shame story can make the breach more damaging than the purchase.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Count the lapse accurately and refuse the all-or-nothing story.
